notable_absence.finding: The schema block at the top of the page (the bracketed JSON skeleton under 'Bootstrap Configuration Schema') lists roughly 90 leaf properties across api/auth/bootstrap/bucket_credentials/database_credentials/logging/replicator/unsupported, but only a fraction have real behavioural constraints (defaults, edition gates, cross-setting minimums) worth modeling as relations - the remainder (most of the logging.* rotation sub-tree: collation_buffer_size, color_enabled, max_age, max_size, rotated_logs_size_limit, rotation_interval, repeated near-identically six times for audit/console/debug/error/info/stats/trace/warn) is a mechanical repeat of the same rotation-policy shape with only the numeric defaults differing. Modeling all six-to-eight repetitions as separate concepts would inflate the registry with near-duplicate 'rotation policy' entries for no ontological gain, so only the settings with a genuinely distinct constraint were extracted; the repeated rotation sub-schema itself is noted here rather than forced into relations.

cross_component_finding: This page's `bootstrap.group_id` setting is the concrete configuration surface behind the abstract sgw:config-group entity introduced on configuration-overview.json - the two pages describe the same mechanism from two directions (overview: what a config group IS and does; this page: the literal field and its default). Similarly, `unsupported.allow_dbconfig_env_vars` directly narrows the scope of configuration-environment-variables.json's sgw:environment-variable-substitution mechanism specifically to database configs, a node-wide kill switch not mentioned on that page at all - this is the clearest example in the batch of a field on one schema page silently gating a mechanism fully documented on a different page, discoverable only by reading both.
cross_product_finding: sgw:bootstrap-server-connection-string's port defaults (11210/11207) and DNS SRV support explicitly reference Couchbase Server's own SDK connection conventions ('Sync Gateway supports the ability to resolve DNS SRV records for alternate hostnames... See the Couchbase Go SDK documentation'), and its alternate-address / NAT handling ('network=external') is structurally identical in shape to xdcr:alternate-address-target (XDCR's own alternate-address targeting for NAT/port-forwarded clusters) - both are a client resolving 'real' vs. 'externally visible' addresses for a remote Couchbase Server cluster. No page in this batch states a relationship between the two, and the underlying products/topologies differ (Sync Gateway-to-Server client connection vs. Server-to-Server XDCR), so they are kept separate, but the mechanism-level echo is worth flagging.
